proposed_waves.rationale: Foundation: every module, plugin, test source set and the TinyHttpd composite build created once so later waves never touch build.gradle/settings.gradle.
Pure routing (Method/MethodSet/Router/RouteBuilder), package com.snoworca.naruserve + internal.router. File-disjoint from wave 3.

Request/Response/BodyState/HttpAdapter SPI + memory test adapter. Declares the full Request/Response/RestApp public surface as signatures (feature methods delegate to stub internal classes) so waves 5-7 add implementations without editing these interfaces. Parallel with wave 2.
All three edit RestApp/DefaultRestApp and the dispatch pipeline; one worker, serial order 5 -> 6 -> 7. Introduces JsonCodec and Logger SPIs.

Serial order 9 -> 10 -> 8: Gson codec, cookies, then TinyHttpd adapter + bootstrap RestApp.create() (which needs the Gson module). Adapter defines streaming/upgrade hooks for later waves. Kept in one worker because create() joins gson+tinyhttpd.
Multipart and static/cache/range: internal.multipart and internal.staticfiles packages + adapter-side file transfer. Parallel with wave 7 if wave-3/5 stubs are in place.
Long-lived connections: WS, SSE, then shutdown/backpressure/load which needs both. internal.ws/internal.sse packages + adapter upgrade/stream files. Parallel with wave 6.

Serial order 16 -> 19 -> 17 -> 18: Kotlin audit + NaruServe-kotlin, optional Servlet adapter, Android sample/QA (separate build), release gate. #19 could be split into its own parallel wave alongside 16 if the 8-wave cap is relaxed.

shared_files.strategy: #1 declares every module block (api, tinyhttpd, gson, bootstrap, kotlin, servlet) with dependencies and test deps up front. Later waves may only append test-only deps; #18 adds SBOM/licence plugins at the end (serial wave 8). Android sample uses its own build files under samples/android (documented exception to 'no per-module build files' because AGP must not be forced on ./gradlew build).

#1 only. includeBuild of TinyHttpd must NOT use a relative '../TinyHttpd' path: worktrees live under .claude/worktrees/<name>, so a relative path breaks. Use a gradle property (e.g. tinyhttpd.dir in gradle.properties / -P) defaulting to /Users/beom/work/git/TinyHttpd, with a clear error if missing. Note parallel worktree builds share TinyHttpd's build dir and Gradle locks; expect waits, not failures.

Wave 3/4 freeze the full interface (all app.* methods from docs/api/app.md) with implementation in DefaultRestApp delegating to per-feature internal classes. Waves 6/7 only edit their own internal.<feature> packages. If a signature change is unavoidable, it goes in the serial wave of its owner and the parallel sibling wave rebases.

Same as RestApp: wave 3 declares all methods; feature methods delegate to internal.json / internal.cookie / internal.multipart / internal.staticfiles / internal.sse helpers. Waves 6 and 7 must stay inside their own packages.

#8 defines the SPI hooks (InputStream body, raw OutputStream/streaming, file transfer, upgrade callback) and splits adapter code into per-feature classes; waves 6/7 add new classes (e.g. TinyHttpdWebSocketBridge, TinyHttpdSseBridge, TinyHttpdFileSender) rather than editing the adapter core.
#1 fixes the module table and dependency snippet; #8 confirms RestApp.create() module; #18 final sweep. Serial by wave order.

Each issue edits only the section(s) for its API and resolves only its own (미확정) markers. Waves 6/7 touch different sections (multipart/static vs ws) — textual merge expected to be clean; orchestrator merges wave 6 before wave 7 if conflict.

One owner per file by scope (response.md shared by #4 base and #12 file section; request.md by #4/#9/#11; lifecycle.md by #6/#15/#17; defaults.md by #8/#15). Shared ones follow section ownership, as for app.md.
#1 creates the Kotlin test source set with one empty test; each feature wave may add its own Kotlin test file (new file per feature, T11 incremental); #16 does the full audit.

Do not block waves 1-7 on this.

notes: Architecture fit: object.md §2.1 logical modules (rest-json/multipart/static/stream) are kept as internal packages inside NaruServe-api rather than separate jars, which §2.1 explicitly allows ('소수 JAR로 패키징'); only things that pull external deps get their own module (tinyhttpd, gson, kotlin, servlet) plus the bootstrap module NaruServe that owns RestApp.create(). Dependency direction is strictly inward to NaruServe-api; nothing in api references TinyHttpd, Gson, android.* or javax.servlet. animal-sniffer API 21 must be applied to api, tinyhttpd, gson, bootstrap and kotlin (currently only api). TinyHttpd has no maven-publish, so composite build (includeBuild + substitution of com.snoworca.tinyhttpd:tinyhttpd-core/-websocket) is the only option without editing TinyHttpd; TinyHttpd already compiles with release 8 and its own API 21 check, and it enforces zero external runtime deps (SEC-16). Biggest parallelism risk is shared interfaces (RestApp/Request/Response/adapter): the plan relies on waves 3-5 freezing the full public surface with per-feature delegation so waves 6 and 7 are file-disjoint. Package root com.snoworca.naruserve matches the existing group in build.gradle; recommend confirming it in #1.
